feedback/alert.notes:
```tsx
<Alert color="brand-purple" icon={sparkles} title="New">Dark theme is here.</Alert>
<Alert dismissable dismissLabel="Close the notice" dismissIcon={check} icon={null}>Saved.</Alert>
<Alert tone="danger" title="Could not load" actionPlacement="below" action={<Button size="sm" onClick={retry}>Retry</Button>}>The server did not answer.</Alert>
<Alert tone="info" dismissable action={[reload]}>A new version is ready.</Alert>
```
feedback/alert.a11y:
`warn` and `danger` alerts have `role="alert"` (announced at once); the others `role="status"` (polite). The dismiss
button is labelled "Dismiss" (translated). Actions are ordinary buttons after the text in the Tab order, before the
dismiss button. The icon is decorative. Colours come from the tone tokens and keep text
contrast in every theme.

Runs on the motion engine; with reduced motion the glyph changes at once
feedback/check-mark.a11y:
The glyph is hidden from assistive technology; the text ("Yes", "No", "Partly", or yours) is what is read, so the
meaning never rests on colour or shape alone. With `label={false}` the whole mark is `aria-hidden`: use that only when
the text around it already says the same (a "not included" note, a checkbox row).

feedback/empty.a11y:
Plain content: the title is a paragraph in the reading order, the icon is decorative, the actions are ordinary buttons
reachable with Tab. Tables and the router use the same `m-empty` look for their own empty states.

feedback/error-box.notes:
Without either, it says "Something went wrong." (translated); `message` replaces that text.

```tsx
<ErrorBox message="We could not reach the server." retry={reconnect} retryLabel="Reconnect" />
```

Parts carry `m-errorbox-title`, `m-errorbox-text` and `m-errorbox-retry` for your own styles.
feedback/error-box.a11y:
`role="alert"`: the error is announced when it appears. The message is text (never HTML from the error). The retry
button is a native button in the reading order.

feedback/live-status.a11y:
`role="status"` with `aria-live`: the text is read when it changes, after what the reader is saying (`polite`) or at
once (`assertive`; keep it for errors). The region must be on the page before its text changes, so render it always
and change only the text. A hidden status is clipped, not `display: none`, so it is still read. The hint line is a
plain paragraph: it is read once, when focus enters the widget that points at it.

feedback/loader.notes:
```tsx
<Loader text="Saving…" color="brand-orange" fade={false} />
<Loader spinner={<Logo />} label="Opening the editor" />
<Loader spinner={false} text="One moment…" />
```

`bootLoader.done({ id = "m-boot", fade = 250 })` returns false when there is no boot element.
feedback/loader.a11y:
`role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`: the text is announced once. The spinner is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
The fade-in waits a moment, so a fast load never flashes a spinner.

feedback/progress.notes:
```tsx
<Progress value={$done} max={8} label="Upload" showValue={(percent, value) => `${value} of 8 files`} />
<Progress value={40} ariaLabel="Storage used" />
<Progress variant="line" value={$read} smooth={false} ariaLabel="Reading progress" />
<Progress variant="line" decorative fillRef={(fill) => scrollIndicator(fill, { track: article })} />
<Progress segments={5} value={$step} valueText={(v, n) => `Step ${v} of ${n}`} />
<Progress variant="line" inverse segments={stories.length} value={$i} duration={6000} paused={$hold} run={story.id} onDone={next} />
```

A line is driven from outside in two ways: a `value` (a signal that follows the scroll, the slide, the step) or
`fillRef`, which hands the fill element to a driver that writes its transform itself. `--m-progress-gap` is the space
between parts and `--m-progress-track` the track colour.
feedback/progress.a11y:
`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow` (absent while indeterminate) and the
label as its name ("Progress" when none). The fill is clipped, not scaled, and mirrors in right-to-left layouts; the
cycle and the indeterminate sweep stop with reduced motion. A timed part keeps its time with reduced motion (it is
information); `decorative` hides the bar when another element already says the progress.

feedback/pull-to-refresh.notes:
```tsx
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={load} icon={rotateCw} color="brand-orange" labels={{ pull: "Pull for new events", refresh: "Load new events" }}>…</PullToRefresh>
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={load} indicator={(phase) => (phase === "ready" ? "↑" : "↓")} settle={false}>…</PullToRefresh>
```

With `refreshButton={false}` give keyboard users another way to refresh.
feedback/pull-to-refresh.a11y:
A visually hidden "Refresh" button appears on focus, so the refresh works from the keyboard. The state ("Pull to
refresh", "Release to refresh", "Refreshing…") is announced in a polite live region and the area is `aria-busy`
while refreshing. The pull only starts at the very top, so normal scrolling (and `touch-action` panning) is untouched;
the click that ends a mouse pull is swallowed. With reduced motion the indicator still spins (it reports progress) but
the content snaps back without a slide.

feedback/skeleton.a11y:
The lines carry `aria-busy="true"` and the label "Loading" (translated); a block and a circle are `aria-hidden` (decorative, the
region around it says it is loading). The shimmer stops with reduced motion.

feedback/spinner.a11y:
`role="status"` with the label as its name, so screen readers hear what is loading. `decorative`
hides it (`aria-hidden`) where a text or a live region next to it already says so. With reduced motion the ring
keeps turning slowly (a still ring reads as "stuck"); the speed follows the motion tokens.

feedback/status-dot.a11y:
With `label` the dot is `role="img"` with that name. Without it the dot is hidden from assistive technology: put the
state in the text beside it, never in the colour alone. The pulse stops under reduced motion.
